title: Knee MRI — fused soft labels (lexicon + open-weights LLM)
subtitle: The union of two report readers, +0.070 macro AUC over either alone
description:
The same twelve soft targets as `knee-phase1-artifacts`, but produced by
**combining two independent readers of the same reports**: the hand-built
multilingual lexicon, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct reading each report into a closed
seven-rung state ladder under a fixed output schema.

**Neither reader wins alone.** Scored on the 58 expert-labelled studies with one
convention: lexicon 0.7446, LLM 0.7421, and a paired bootstrap puts the
difference between them at -0.0025, CI [-0.060, +0.049] — not separated.

**The union beats both: 0.8145**, paired difference +0.0698 over the lexicon,
CI [+0.041, +0.097]. They combine because they fail on different findings; the
LLM is far better on Medial Meniscus, Medial OA and Lateral OA and far worse on
Fracture, PF OA and Contusion.

**The combination rule has no free parameters**, deliberately: exactly one
reader speaks, take it; both speak, average their ranks; neither, abstain. A
rule that picked the better reader per finding would be fitting twelve choices
to 58 studies and would report a number that means nothing.

Supervision rises from 50.6% of study-by-finding slots to 65.4%. Adds a
`__weight` column per finding — a confidence that scales that target's
contribution to the loss, so an explicit severe finding counts for more than a
hedge.

**Two layers, deliberately:** the model picks from a closed vocabulary and
Python maps vocabulary to numbers. A model is good at choosing from a fixed set
and bad at emitting calibrated probabilities, and a confident wrong number is
not catchable downstream.

**Compliance:** the reader is open-weights and ran inside a Kaggle kernel. No
report text was sent to any hosted LLM API, and none is present in these files.

**Access:** private. Keyed by competition StudyInstanceUIDs; competition-derived
data may not be redistributed.

resources.description: One row per training study (4,407). Twelve soft target scores, one per finding, plus a five-way supervision channel per finding recording HOW each score was reached: asserted, hedged, low_severity, negated, or absent. `absent` means the labeler had nothing to say, and training masks the loss on those rather than teaching them as negatives — a report that never mentions the ACL is not a report saying the ACL is intact. Also carries the detected report language. No report text.

fields.description: Soft score in [0,1], or null where the labeler abstained

resources.description: DICOM header scan over 24,386 series and 819,635 slices, headers only — no pixels were read. Carries pixel spacing, slice counts, laterality, anatomical plane and the scanner fields used to build the fold-grouping fingerprint. Grouping on that fingerprint matters: random K-fold inflates macro AUC by 0.087 on this dataset, because no site column exists anywhere and the scanner is the leak.
